title: Trombone lessons at Juilliard
summary: A Met Opera first-chair teacher told him to choose between money and learning the trombone, and said they would work on what comes out of the horn. He developed a classical sound.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah. The sad thing is that when I went to Juilliard, I’m finally in this wonderful school. I have this teacher that is the best and he plays the first chair at the Metropolitan Orchestra. The first lesson he says, “Okay Mac, before we play a not let’s get something straight.” He says, “Do you want to learn to play the trombone or do you want to make money?” He says, “Because, I’m going to tell you, if you want to make money you’ll earn more by the time you learn to really play the trombone,” He says, “You could have made tons of money selling tomatoes.” He says, “So you have to decide now, do you want to make money or do you want to learn to play the trombone.” I laughed and I said, “I’m here to play the trombone.” He said, “Let’s get started.” He was a wonderful teacher. I mention him because now that he accepted me as a teacher, I’m sure that I’m finally going to learn how to get this thing settled, the embrasure. I said, “I’m self-taught and I never really got the embrasure set.” He looked me and laughed and said, “Mac, I’m just like you. I’m self-taught. I never concerned myself with embrasure and all that. I’m a musician and I deal with what comes out of the horn, that’s all I teach. We’ll deal with what comes out of your horn.” So, the next thing I knew, I was developing a very good sound. I could see that the first thing you have to do is get the sound the instrument was designed for. He taught me how to do that. The next thing I knew, around New York, all the bands wanted me to play in their bands because I had a good sound. I was sounding like a classical player playing jazz with a classical sound.
